title: DV Arrest, Complaint and Weapon Seizure
key_points: Arrest and sign a complaint are MANDATORY when probable cause of DV exists and: the victim shows signs of injury; a warrant is in effect; there is probable cause a served restraining order was violated (2C:29-9); or a weapon (2C:39-1) was involved.
Otherwise, arrest and/or signing a complaint is discretionary when probable cause of DV exists.
Signs of injury are read broadly and include pain or impaired condition; if both parties are hurt, weigh comparative injuries, DV history and other factors to find the primary victim.
A victim who used reasonable force in self-defense may not be arrested or charged for it.

Ask whether weapons are on the premises; seize any weapon that puts the victim at risk of serious bodily injury, and with a firearm also seize the FPIC and handgun purchase permits. Send items to the county prosecutor and inventory them in the DV report.
officer_notes: If the victim has no copy of the order, confirm it with the issuing agency.
Follow the AG Domestic Violence Procedures Manual for reporting and victim notice.

subsections.label: a
subsections.text: Mandatory arrest and complaint when probable cause of DV exists and the victim shows signs of injury, a warrant is in effect, a restraining order violation occurred, or a weapon was involved

subsections.label: b
subsections.text: Discretionary arrest and complaint in other cases with probable cause

subsections.label: c
subsections.text: When both parties are injured, weigh comparative injuries, history and other factors; do not arrest a victim for reasonable self-defense

subsections.label: d
subsections.text: Ask about and seize weapons at risk; seize FPIC and permits with any firearm; forward to the county prosecutor
